subject: Request: temporary SLA exception for MajorCloud migration
messages:
From: Tina Huang <tina@majorcloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Migration window — request for temporary SLA flexibility

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare for our MajorCloud data center migration (planned cutover across Dec 20–28), procurement asked us to get an official, short-term SLA exception documented. Our ask: for the first 90 days post-cutover we need a temporary adjustment to the standard availability target and a modified credit schedule.

Specifically:
- Proposed temporary uptime target: 99.5% (vs your standard 99.9%) for a 90-day stabilization window
- Reduced monthly service credits (capped at a one-time 10% credit for the billing month impacted)
- Exclude planned migration windows (we expect a series of short cutovers and a couple of maintenance windows totalling ~36–48 hours spread over three weeks) from uptime calculations

We understand this is non-standard; MajorCloud can accept tighter operational guardrails if you need them (e.g., additional reporting, an escalation contact, and a 24/7 on-call during the migration).

Attachments: MAJCLOUD-migration-plan-logs.zip (migration schedule + preliminary impact analysis)

Can you confirm if Redwood can accept a temporary exception along these lines, and what changes you would require in the SLA wording? Procurement would like this in writing for our change approval workflow.

Thanks — Tina
Tina Huang
Head of Cloud Platform Operations | MajorCloud

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Huang <tina@majorcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Migration window — request for temporary SLA flexibility

Hi Tina — thanks for the clear note and the migration packet. We're sympathetic to the migration risk and happy to work through a temporary template exception, subject to a couple constraints.

High-level, we can consider a 90-day stabilization amendment. Questions/constraints from our side:
- We'd prefer a compromise uptime of 99.6% (not as low as 99.5%) for the stabilization window, paired with a modest credit cap.
- Credits: Redwood typically calculates credits as a function of downtime bands. For a temporary exception, we can cap the total monthly credit exposure to 5% of the monthly invoice for the affected billing period; incremental credits above that would require exec sign-off.
- Scheduled migration/maintenance: we can exclude planned migration windows if events are scheduled and agreed in advance (DocuSign sign-off plus a rolling notification 72 hrs before each event).
- Latency: we cannot relax tail-latency SLOs aggressively. Suggest keeping the 95th percentile target, but we can add a higher latency forgiveness bucket for the migration window (e.g., 95th up to 150ms tolerated with reporting).

I'll loop in Legal (Laura) and our Solutions lead (Marissa) to draft a concrete amendment. Attaching a working draft SLA with inline comments — see 20261210_sla-exception-draft.pdf.

Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T08:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Migration window — request for temporary SLA flexibility

Looping in a few practical considerations from ops:
- We can accept 99.6% for 90 days, but for MajorCloud's scale we should add a per-region carve-out rule so a single region migration doesn't reduce global availability calculations unexpectedly.
- Credit calculation: instead of a flat 5% cap, propose a tiered cap tied to severity banding:
  * Severity 1 (platform down): credits per standard band up to 5% cap
  * Severity 2 (degraded latency impacting >20% of calls): tighter per-incident credits with an aggregated cap of 7%
This keeps alignment with our risk while giving MajorCloud material remediation if something goes wrong.
- Reporting: require daily migration health reports during the cutover window and a post-migration incident report within 5 business days for any SLO breach.

I'll add these into the draft and flag the per-region wording.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Migration window — request for temporary SLA flexibility

Legal redlines (high level):
- We will allow a 90-day stabilization amendment, but we need:
  1) a mutual definition of "planned migration windows" (specific datestamps + UTC windows) to avoid ambiguity;
  2) a clause that limits the exclusion to explicitly scheduled events and forbids retroactive exclusions for unplanned outages;
  3) an overall credit cap per billing period (we agree 5% but would accept up to 7% only with Exec approval).
- Add an audit log clause: MajorCloud must provide access to migration logs and support traces on request to validate claims for credits.
- DocuSign: include a signature block that references amendment ID (we'll use AMEND-DEAL-8932).

I can redline the PDF and return.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Tina Huang <tina@majorcloud.com>, Alan Chesworth <procure@majorcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed temporary SLA amendment (MajorCloud) — draft attached

Tina / Alan — thanks for your patience while we reviewed internally. Attached is Redwood's proposed temporary amendment for the 90-day stabilization period post-cutover (2026-12-20 through 2027-03-19, inclusive). Summary of the proposal:

- Uptime target: 99.6% for the 90-day stabilization window (compromise from your 99.5% ask).
- Credit structure: standard downtime bands remain in place; total credit exposure for any single billing month impacted by the migration is capped at 5% of that month’s invoice.
- Severity banding: per-incident credits apply as normal; in the event of multiple incidents in the window, aggregated credits are subject to the monthly cap.
- Scheduled migration exclusions: up to 72 hours of pre-scheduled, mutually-agreed maintenance/cutover time may be excluded from uptime calculations if scheduled in advance and confirmed by DocuSign. Any additional unscheduled outages are treated per standard SLA.
- Latency forgiveness: during scheduled migration windows only, 95th percentile latency of up to 150ms will be reported but not counted as an SLO breach; all other latency degradations remain reportable and remediable.
- Regional carve-out: exclusions apply to the impacted region(s) only; global availability calculations will use region-aware aggregation to avoid skew in unaffected regions.
- Reporting & evidence: MajorCloud must provide migration logs and daily health reports during the cutover and submit any credit claims within 30 days with supporting evidence. Redwood reserves the right to validate claims and request additional logs.

Attached: 20261214_sla-exception-draft.pdf (clean copy) and MAJCLOUD-migration-plan-logs.zip (submitted earlier). If this is acceptable, please countersign the amendment via DocuSign (link below) and we'll publish AMEND-DEAL-8932 under your account.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/MAJCLOUD-SLA-8932
Drive: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/MAJCLOUD-migration-logs

If you need to preserve additional protections (e.g., higher credit caps or different uptime targets), let us know and we can escalate to Exec review for approval.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Tina Huang <tina@majorcloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Chesworth <procure@majorcloud.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed temporary SLA amendment (MajorCloud) — draft attached

Karthik — thank you. The amendment looks reasonable and aligns with what procurement anticipated. We'll run this through our change approval and the procurement committee; I expect to have a countersigned DocuSign back by Tuesday (2026-12-21) assuming no further legal concerns.

Two quick asks we may include in signatures:
1) Can Redwood provide a named escalation contact during the cutover (24/7 on-call)?
2) Can we get an example post-migration incident report template so our teams align on data fields?

If those are straightforward, we can attach them to the signed amendment.

Thanks — Tina
